title: Emergence of cooperation: A reputation-modulated reinforcement learning
abstract: arXiv:2608.20016v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Reputation is widely recognized as a key mechanism for sustaining cooperation. However, most existing game-theoretic models treat reputation primarily as an external factor that modulates payoffs, interaction structures, or strategy update rules. In many social contexts, though, reputation operates primarily as information -- it shapes how individuals interpret their own experiences and assess the behavior of others. To bridge this gap, we propose a spatial prisoner's dilemma game grounded in the reinforcement learning paradigm, in which agents equipped with Q-learning integrate both individual and social information via a locally defined reputation metric to guide their decisions. Our results reveal that reputation-modulated learning significantly promotes the emergence of cooperative behavior, and we observe a discontinuous phase transition from full cooperation to full defection as the temptation increases. translated_title: 合作的涌现：一种声誉调制的强化学习
translated_abstract: 声誉被广泛认为是维持合作的关键机制。然而，大多数现有的博弈论模型主要将声誉视为一种外部因素，用于调节收益、交互结构或策略更新规则。在许多社会情境中，声誉主要作为信息运作——它塑造个体如何解读自身经验并评估他人行为。为弥合这一差距，我们提出了一种基于强化学习范式的空间囚徒困境博弈，其中配备Q学习的智能体通过局部定义的声誉指标整合个体和社会信息以指导其决策。我们的结果表明，声誉调制的学习显著促进了合作行为的涌现，并且随着诱惑增加，我们观察到从完全合作到完全背叛的不连续相变。合作通过声誉机制在空间中传播。
tldr: 本文提出一种基于声誉调制的Q学习空间囚徒困境模型，发现声誉作为信息能显著促进合作涌现，并导致合作到背叛的不连续相变。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a reputation-modulated Q-learning spatial prisoner's dilemma model, showing that reputation as information significantly promotes cooperation emergence and induces a discontinuous phase transition from cooperation to defection.
